html:
The K'iche' are a Maya people of the western highlands of Guatemala and the largest Maya group there today. In 1492 they ruled the strongest kingdom in the highlands.

Their capital was Q'umarkaj, also called Utatlán, near modern Santa Cruz del Quiché. The kingdom reached its height in the 1400s under the king K'iq'ab, when it held much of the highlands. Later in that century the Kaqchikel broke away and became rivals. In 1524 the conquistador Pedro de Alvarado defeated the K'iche' near Quetzaltenango, then burned Q'umarkaj and its kings.

Their sacred book, the Popol Vuh, was written down in K'iche' in Latin letters in the 1550s and tells of the creation of people from maize and the deeds of the Hero Twins. The name Guatemala comes from the Nahuatl for "place of many trees", a translation of K'iche'. The activist Rigoberta Menchú, winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992, is K'iche'. Their ancestors belong to the late phase of the Maya city-states.
sum: The K'iche' are a Maya people of the western highlands of Guatemala and the largest Maya group there today. In 1492 they ruled the strongest kingdom in the highlands.
